data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: activity
sections.summary: Something that you do for enjoyment, exercise or a specific purpose; also the state in which a lot of things are happening.

senses.definition: something that you do for interest or pleasure, or as part of your job or daily life
examples: Swimming is an excellent physical activity that benefits both your body and your mental health.

senses.definition: the situation in which a lot of things are happening or people are moving around
examples: There was a great deal of activity in the school corridor between lessons.

answers.answer: The sports centre offers a wide range of activities for all ages, from yoga to rock climbing.
She showed great activity in solving the maths problem on the board without any assistance.
He had a lot of activity in his school bag that he carried to every afternoon lesson.
The activity was very soft and warm, making it perfect to use in the bedroom during winter.

sections.question: concert
sections.summary: A live performance of music played in front of an audience, usually at a specific venue.

senses.definition: a live performance of music in front of an audience
examples: She bought tickets to a concert by her favourite band almost six months in advance.

senses.definition: used in the phrase 'in concert' meaning working together or performing live
examples: The two companies acted in concert to reduce their environmental impact.

answers.answer: The outdoor concert attracted over twenty thousand people despite the cold weather.
He had a long concert with his manager to discuss the details of the new project.
She showed great concert in completing all her assignments well ahead of each deadline.
The concert was so heavy that it took three people to lift it onto the stage.

sections.question: entertainment
sections.summary: Shows, performances, films or other activities that people enjoy watching or taking part in; also the act of keeping people entertained or hosting guests.

senses.definition: shows, performances or activities that people enjoy watching or participating in
examples: The festival offered a wide variety of entertainment, including live music, comedy and dance.

senses.definition: the act of hosting guests and making them feel welcome
examples: The company provided entertainment for its clients at the annual summer dinner.

answers.answer: The theme park offers entertainment for the whole family, from rides to live shows.
She showed great entertainment in completing all the exercises before the end of the lesson.
He had entertainment in his school bag to keep him occupied on the long coach journey.
The entertainment was very soft and warm, making everyone feel comfortable and relaxed.

sections.question: hobby
sections.summary: An activity that you enjoy doing regularly in your free time, not as your main job.

senses.definition: an activity that you enjoy doing regularly in your spare time, outside of work
examples: Photography became her hobby after she received a camera as a birthday present.

answers.answer: He took up running as a hobby and eventually completed his first half-marathon last spring.
She had great hobby for mathematics and always arrived early to every lesson without fail.
He put the hobby in his bag and brought it to the afternoon lesson to show the teacher.
The class showed great hobby in finishing the group project several days before the deadline.

sections.question: leisure
sections.summary: Free time when you are not working and can do activities you enjoy; also used as an adjective to describe relaxed, unhurried activities or spaces.

senses.definition: time when you are free from work or other duties and can relax or do things you enjoy
examples: She spends her leisure time reading, painting and visiting art galleries across the city.

senses.definition: used to describe activities or facilities designed for enjoyment and relaxation
examples: The new leisure centre has a swimming pool, gym and indoor climbing wall.

answers.answer: At leisure, she enjoys gardening, walking in the countryside and learning new languages.
He showed great leisure in completing the difficult assignment well before the submission deadline.
She packed her leisure carefully into her suitcase for the two-week holiday in the south of France.
The leisure was very informative and helped the students understand a particularly difficult topic.

sections.question: museum
sections.summary: A building where interesting and important historical, scientific or artistic objects are collected, kept and displayed for the public to see.

senses.definition: a building in which objects of historical, scientific or artistic importance are collected, kept and put on display for the public
examples: The class visited a natural history museum to study prehistoric animals and fossils.

answers.answer: The city's science museum attracts over a million visitors from around the world each year.
She watched a museum on television about the history of ancient Egypt on Saturday evening.
He kept a small museum in his school bag that he referred to during every history lesson.
The museum was very tasty and all the students thoroughly enjoyed it at the end-of-term party.

sections.question: performance
sections.summary: The act of performing a play, concert, dance or other show in front of an audience; also how well a person or thing does something.

senses.definition: the act of performing a play, concert or other entertainment in front of an audience
examples: The audience gave the cast a standing ovation at the end of the final performance.

senses.definition: how well or badly a person, machine or organisation does something
examples: The manager reviewed each team member's performance at the end of the financial year.

answers.answer: The evening performance of the ballet was sold out weeks before opening night.
She had a long performance with her teacher about the essay she had submitted a week late.
He packed his performance carefully into his bag and handed it to the director before leaving.
The performance was very soft and comfortable and helped everyone relax after the long working day.

sections.question: recreation
sections.summary: Activities done for enjoyment and relaxation when not working; leisure activities that refresh the body or mind.

senses.definition: activities that people do for enjoyment when they are not working
examples: The park provides excellent facilities for outdoor recreation, including walking trails and sports courts.

answers.answer: The town built a new recreation centre with a swimming pool, gym and indoor sports hall.
The class did a careful recreation of the experiment to verify that the original results were accurate.
She showed great recreation in solving the problem on the board and explaining it to the class.
He had a lot of recreation in his backpack that he used during the afternoon science lesson.

sections.question: theatre
sections.summary: A building where plays and other live performances are staged; also the art of writing and performing plays; also used to refer to an operating theatre in a hospital.

senses.definition: a building with a stage where plays, musicals and other live performances are presented to an audience
examples: She has loved going to the theatre ever since she saw her first play at the age of eight.

senses.definition: plays and other dramatic works as an art form
examples: He studied theatre at drama school before beginning his career as an actor.

senses.definition: (UK) a room in a hospital where surgical operations are performed
examples: The patient was taken to theatre early in the morning for the operation.

answers.answer: The local theatre is staging a new production of Hamlet every evening throughout October.
He watched a theatre on television about the history of the Second World War last night.
She bought a theatre from the supermarket and prepared it carefully for the family dinner.
He was very theatre at the school play, performing his role with total confidence on stage.

sections.question: tourism
sections.summary: The activity of travelling to places for pleasure or interest; also the business of providing services for people who travel.

senses.definition: the activity of travelling to places away from home for pleasure or interest
examples: Tourism is one of the most important industries in many coastal regions of the world.

senses.definition: the business of organising and providing services for tourists
examples: The country invested heavily in tourism after a report showed its potential for economic growth.

answers.answer: The region depends heavily on tourism, with millions of visitors arriving each summer.
She showed great tourism during the geography lesson and answered every question correctly.
He had tourism in his school bag that he used to plan the route to the national museum.
The class did a tourism together after the geography exam to celebrate the end of term.
